appsec.title: Application Security — 30 Day Interview Prep Roadmap
appsec.subtitle: For entry-to-associate level AppSec interviews. Assumes prior security exposure. ~1.5–2 hours/day. All resources are free.
appsec.audience: You already have AppSec experience. This roadmap fills the structured-revision and interview-pattern gaps.

project.title: Vulnerable REST API + AI-Assisted Code Review
project.tagline: Build a deliberately vulnerable API, then use Claude Code to do a structured security review and publish the writeup.
project.stand_out: Demonstrates offensive understanding + defensive code review + AI fluency in one artefact. Recruiters see all three on one GitHub repo.
steps: Day 1–3: Build a Node.js (Express) or Python (FastAPI) REST API with auth, profile endpoints, file upload, search. Intentionally introduce: IDOR, SQL injection, JWT alg:none, SSRF in URL-fetch endpoint, mass assignment, missing rate limit on login, XXE in XML upload.
Day 4–6: Use Claude Code or any LLM to do a 'security code review' — prompt it to walk every endpoint and rate findings. Capture its output verbatim.
Day 7: Write a 'AI-assisted vs manual' comparison post: what the AI caught, what it missed, what it false-flagged. This is the differentiator — it shows judgement, not just output.
Day 8: Publish the repo with a README structured like a pentest report (executive summary + findings + fixes). Cross-post the writeup on Medium and LinkedIn.
Bonus: add a fix-PR for each finding so the same repo shows secure-coding patterns next to the vulnerable original.
deliverables: README written as a pentest report
Medium / LinkedIn post: 'I asked Claude Code to security-review my vulnerable API — here is what it caught and missed'
Linked from your CV under Projects

grc.title: Governance & ISO 27001 — 30 Day Interview Prep Roadmap
grc.subtitle: Entry-to-associate ISO 27001 + GRC roles. Targets DORA/GDPR-adjacent Irish FS market. ~1.5 hours/day. All resources free.
grc.audience: You have technical security background. This roadmap converts it into GRC vocabulary, frameworks, and interview confidence.

project.title: Mini ISMS for a Fictional SaaS — Built with AI
project.tagline: A full starter ISMS for an imaginary Dublin-based fintech (gdpr + DORA in scope), drafted with AI assistance and hand-tailored.
project.stand_out: Most GRC junior candidates can recite ISO 27001 clauses. Almost none can show a complete documented ISMS. This is your differentiator.
steps: Day 1–3: Pick a fictional company. Define scope: 30-person SaaS in Dublin, processes EU customer data, sells to FS. Document the org context + interested parties (Clause 4).

Day 4–7: Use Claude Code to draft the core policy stack (information security policy, access control, asset management, supplier security, incident management, business continuity). Hand-edit every one — AI gets you 70% there, your judgement gets you the last 30%.
Day 8–12: Build the risk register: 20 risks with likelihood × impact, treatment decisions, owner, review date. Use the 5×5 matrix.
Day 13–16: Build the Statement of Applicability for all 93 Annex A controls (2022 edition). Mark applicable/not + justification.
Day 17–20: Add the operational artefacts: asset inventory template, incident response runbook, internal audit programme, management review template.
Day 21–23: Map your controls to DORA articles (Articles 5–15) so the same ISMS evidences DORA readiness too.
Day 24–28: Publish to a public GitHub repo with a clean README explaining how AI accelerated drafting and what you tailored manually.
Day 29–30: Write a Medium post: 'I built a full ISMS for a fictional fintech using AI — here is what I learned about GRC craft'.
deliverables: Full policy stack (10+ documents) in Markdown
Statement of Applicability (Annex A 2022) as a spreadsheet
Medium / LinkedIn post explaining your approach

ai_security.title: AI / LLM Security — 30 Day Interview Prep Roadmap
ai_security.subtitle: For AI/LLM Security and AI Red Team roles. Fastest-growing security niche. ~1.5–2 hours/day. All resources free.
ai_security.audience: You have AppSec background. This roadmap bridges into AI-specific threats — the field where supply is thin and demand is exploding.

project.title: Vulnerable LLM Agent + Multi-Tool Red Team Writeup
project.tagline: Build a RAG-powered LLM agent with realistic tools, then red-team it with Garak + PyRIT + promptfoo + manual probing. Ship the kill chains.
project.stand_out: AI security candidates rarely have hands-on artefacts — most can recite OWASP LLM Top 10 but cannot demonstrate exploitation or defence. A working repo with documented attack chains, automated tooling, and proposed fixes puts you in the top 5%.
steps: Day 1–4: Build a Python LLM agent using LangChain or LlamaIndex with: (a) a RAG index of fake company docs, (b) a fake email-send tool, (c) a fake SQL query tool, (d) a fake HTTP fetch tool. Use a free model (Llama 3 via Groq free tier, Gemini free tier, or Claude API free credits).

Day 5–8: Seed indirect prompt injection by adding a poisoned doc to the RAG index. Demonstrate the agent calling the email tool to exfiltrate other docs based on the injection. Record the full conversation.
Day 9–12: Run Garak against your agent's exposed prompt endpoint. Capture all probe results. Pick the 3 most interesting and write deep writeups.
Day 13–15: Run PyRIT for multi-turn attack orchestration. Document where automated red teaming beats manual and vice versa.
Day 16–18: Use promptfoo to write 20 declarative security regression tests that any future fix should pass.

Day 19–22: Implement defences: input/output guardrails (LlamaGuard or simple regex), least-privilege tool scoping, human-in-the-loop on high-impact tools, RAG retrieval-layer authZ. Re-run all tools, show before/after.
Day 23–26: Write the whitepaper-style README: threat model diagram, 5 documented attack chains, defence implementation, residual risks, automated regression test suite.
Day 27–28: Cross-post on Medium and LinkedIn. Submit as a talk proposal to BSides Dublin or OWASP Dublin chapter.
deliverables: 5+ documented prompt injection / agent-abuse kill chains
BSides / OWASP chapter talk proposal submitted
